```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Hendriks BS, Reynolds JG, Klinz SG, et al. Multiscale kinetic
  modeling of liposomal doxorubicin delivery quantifies the role of tumor and
  drug-specific parameters in local delivery to tumors. CPT Pharmacometrics
  Syst Pharmacol. 2012;1(11):e15.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/psp.2012.16> (open access,
  PMC3600732)
* Packaged models:
  * `Hendriks_2012_doxorubicin_liposomal_mouse_qsp` -- the mouse model the
    paper trained on literature PK and tumor-deposition data.
  * `Hendriks_2012_doxorubicin_liposomal_human_qsp` -- the human scale-up.

```{r load-models}
mod_mouse <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Hendriks_2012_doxorubicin_liposomal_mouse_qsp"))
mod_human <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Hendriks_2012_doxorubicin_liposomal_human_qsp"))
```

Hendriks 2012 built a multiscale model of how conventional doxorubicin and
pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD) reach the DNA of tumor cells. The
whole-body layer is deliberately minimal: free doxorubicin follows a
two-compartment PK model, PLD a one-compartment model, and the two share the
blood volume as their central compartment so that doxorubicin released from
liposomes joins the free-drug pool. A perfused, well-mixed tumor is attached
to the blood by blood flow; inside it, drug and liposomes cross the capillary
wall by a transvascular flux per unit capillary surface area, liposomes are
taken into tumor cells by fluid-phase uptake and release their doxorubicin,
and free doxorubicin enters the cells through a modified Eytan-Kuchel
membrane model (partition into the outer leaflet, flippase transport to the
inner leaflet, release into the cytosol, reversible DNA binding). The paper
uses the area under the DNA-bound doxorubicin curve as its delivery metric.

The authors published the complete SimBiology model as SBML (one file for
mouse, one for human) together with a parameter and reaction workbook for
each. Those files contain a heart sub-model built exactly like the tumor
sub-model (from the authors' companion cardiac work); it is part of the
published model and is included in both packaged models, since its blood
flow returns drug to the circulation.

# Population

The mouse model was trained on group-mean literature data rather than on
individual animals: plasma PK of free doxorubicin (0.5-20 mg/kg IV) and of
~100 nm pegylated liposomes (3-20 mg/kg doxorubicin basis), and tumor
deposition time courses in subcutaneous xenografts (HepG2, Li-7, BT-474, 4T1,
NCI-N87 for doxorubicin; BT-474, NCI-N87, KB, A375, B16F10, HepG2, Li-7, 4T1
and M190-FR for liposomes), all normalised to percent injected dose
(Figure 3a-f). The cellular parameters `kf_ol` and `kflippase_out` are the
medians of fits to doxorubicin uptake time courses in 21 cancer cell lines
(Figure 2).

The human model scales the mouse model to a 70 kg, 1.8 m^2 adult with a
20 g tumor. Free-doxorubicin PK was re-fitted to pooled clinical PK data
(Figure 3g), liposome elimination to the 111In-PLD data of Harrington et
al. (Figure 3h), the doxorubicin tumor-to-capillary flux to the Kaposi
sarcoma tumor data of Northfelt et al., and the doxorubicin
capillary-to-tumor flux was fixed from DCE-MRI Ktrans values. All cellular,
release and liposome transport parameters were carried from the mouse
model; the liposome tumor influx was estimated per patient (Figure 3l).

Both models are deterministic typical-value models with no between-subject
variability and no residual error.

# Units and dosing

Time is in minutes. States are amounts in nmol of doxorubicin; the liposome
(`*_lipo`) and empty-lipid (`*_lipid`) states are in doxorubicin-equivalent
nmol, so a PLD dose is entered as the nmol of doxorubicin it contains
(20,000 doxorubicin molecules per liposome). Free doxorubicin is dosed into
`central`, PLD into `central_lipo`. Concentrations are nM; tumor and heart
readouts are in ug doxorubicin per g tissue.

```{r dose-helpers}
mw_dox <- 580 # g/mol, as in the published model code
nmol_from_mg <- function(mg) mg / 1e3 / mw_dox * 1e9
mouse_dose <- function(mg_per_kg, wt = 0.02) nmol_from_mg(mg_per_kg * wt)
human_dose <- function(mg_per_m2, bsa = 1.8) nmol_from_mg(mg_per_m2 * bsa)
mouse_dose(3)
human_dose(40)
```

The mouse model code gives the dose as an instantaneous bolus into blood;
the human model code infuses it over 60 minutes. The simulations below
follow the same conventions.

# Source trace

Structure (all equations follow the reaction list of the published SBML
model and workbook; rates are amount per minute):

| Element | Source |
|---|---|
| Two-compartment free doxorubicin PK in blood volume (`kel`, `k12`, `k21`) | Methods 'Combined PK model'; Figure 1a; SBML reactions rxn6, rxn7 |
| One-compartment liposome PK sharing the central compartment (`kel_lipo`) | Methods 'Combined PK model'; SBML rxn2 |
| Optional liposome peripheral compartment (human, `k12_lipo = 0`) | Human SBML / workbook; Methods 'Human scale-up' |
| Release of 20,000 doxorubicin per liposome in blood/capillary, interstitium and cells (`krel_plasma`, `krel_tissue`, `krel_cell`) | Methods; SBML rxn38-rxn44 |
| Empty lipid tracked and cleared like intact liposomes | SBML lipid reactions |
| Tumor and heart: blood flow in, flow minus lymph out, lymph from interstitium | Methods 'Tumor deposition model'; SBML rxn25-rxn33 (tumor), rxn12-rxn20 (heart) |
| Transvascular flux = tvf x capillary surface area density x tissue weight x concentration | Methods; SBML rxn27, rxn32 |
| Capillary surface area and vascular fraction from MVD and a radius distribution | SBML initial assignments `capillarysurfacearea_tumor`, `tumor_frxnvascularvol` |
| Interstitial / cellular split of the non-vascular volume | SBML `tumor_frxninterstitialvol`, `tumor_frxncellvol` |
| Fluid-phase liposome uptake `ke_fluidphase x Ncells x C_int` | Methods; SBML |
| Exocytosis of internalised liposomes and lipid (`kdeg_lipo`) | Workbook; SBML |
| Membrane partition, flippase and cytosol exchange | Methods 'Doxorubicin cellular transport model'; Figure 1b; SBML |
| DNA binding with `kf = kr_DNA / Kd_DNA`; free sites depleted from `Nnuc x 0.18 / NA` per cell | Methods; Table 1; SBML rxn4 and initial assignment of `DNA` |
| Doxorubicin degradation in heart interstitium (`kdeg_dox`) | Workbook; SBML |
| Readouts (`Cc`, `tumor_total_dox`, `tumor_dna_dox`, ...) | SBML repeated assignments |

Parameter values (Table 1 reports lengths in cm; the model works in dm, so
1 cm/min = 0.1 dm/min):

| Parameter | Mouse | Human | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kel`, `k12`, `k21` (1/min) | 0.36, 0.74, 0.0055 | 0.0820, 0.0475, 0.00125 | Table 1 (Fit) |
| `kel_lipo` (1/min) | 0.001141 | 1.67e-4 | Table 1 (Fit); human workbook 1.689e-4 |
| `krel_plasma`, `krel_tissue`, `krel_cell` (1/min) | 5.465e-5, 1.77e-4, 9.6e-4 | same | Methods; Table 1 |
| `ke_fluidphase` (L/min/cell) | 4e-14 | same | Table 1 |
| `kdeg_lipo` (1/min) | 0.0042 | same | Workbooks |
| `tvf_in_tumor_dox` (dm/min) | 2.96e-5 | 3.63e-4 | Table 1 (mouse Fit; human Ktrans) |
| `tvf_out_tumor_dox` (dm/min) | 1.1771e-4 | 8.45e-5 | Table 1 (mouse); human workbook and SBML (see Errata) |
| `tvf_in_tumor_lipo`, `tvf_out_tumor_lipo` (dm/min) | 2.64e-7, 7.14e-7 | same | Table 1 |
| `kf_ol` (dm/min), `kflippase_in`, `kflippase_out` (1/min) | 3.3e-6, 1, 0.37 | same | Table 1 |
| Partition coefficient, leaflet volume fractions | 40,000; 5e-5; 5e-5 | same | Table 1 |
| `Kd_DNA` (nM), `kr_DNA` (1/min) | 1000, 1200 | same | Table 1 |
| Nucleotides per cell, sites per nucleotide | 4.58e7, 0.18 | same | Table 1 |
| Blood volume (L) | 0.0012 | 4.85 | Table 1 (0.06 L/kg x 0.02 kg); human workbook |
| Tumor weight (kg), `Qtumor` (L/min/kg), `Ltumor` | 8.6e-5, 0.21186, 0 | 0.02, 0.0282, 0 | Table 1; workbooks |
| MVD (1/mm^2), capillary radii (3, 5, 7, 23 um) and fractions (0.1, 0.6, 0.2, 0.1) | 250 | same | Table 1; workbooks |
| Cell fraction of non-vascular tumor volume, tumor cell radius | 0.412, 8.5 um | same | Table 1; workbooks |
| Heart weight (kg), `Qheart`, `Lheart` (L/min/kg) | 1.33e-4, 2.105, 7.5e-5 | 0.33, 0.727, 7.5e-5 | Workbooks |
| Heart MVD, capillary radius, cell fraction, myocyte radius | 1650, 2.2 um, 0.849, 15.6 um | same | Workbooks |
| Heart `tvf` (dox in, dox out, lipo in, lipo out; dm/min) | 6.229e-5, 3.571e-5, 2.65e-8, 0 | 3.63e-4, 2.086e-4, 2.65e-8, 0 | Workbooks |
| `kdeg_dox` (1/min), residual blood fraction | 0.014, 0.5 | same | Workbooks |

# Mouse: tumor compartments after 3 mg/kg (Supplementary Figure S2B)

```{r mouse-sim}
tgrid <- c(0, 1, 5, 10, 30, seq(60, 168 * 60, by = 60))
solve_one <- function(mod, cmt, amt, dur = 0, params = NULL, times = tgrid) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = amt, cmt = cmt, dur = dur) |>
    rxode2::et(times, cmt = "central")
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, params = params, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8)
  out <- as.data.frame(out)
  out$h <- out$time / 60
  out
}
m_conv <- solve_one(mod_mouse, "central", mouse_dose(3))
m_lipo <- solve_one(mod_mouse, "central_lipo", mouse_dose(3))
# Conventional arm repeated with the published model code's tumor influx
# flux (6.23e-5 dm/min) instead of Table 1 (2.96e-5 dm/min); see Errata.
m_conv_code <- solve_one(mod_mouse, "central", mouse_dose(3), params = c(tvf_in_tumor_dox = 6.23e-5))
```

```{r mouse-s2b, fig.height = 6}
tumor_long <- function(d, label) {
  d |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      h,
      `Capillary doxorubicin` = c_cap_tumor_dox,
      `Interstitium doxorubicin` = c_int_tumor_dox,
      `Cell doxorubicin, free` = c_cell_tumor_free,
      `Cell doxorubicin, DNA-bound` = c_cell_tumor_bound,
      `Capillary liposomes (dox eq.)` = c_cap_tumor_lipo,
      `Interstitium liposomes (dox eq.)` = c_int_tumor_lipo
    ) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-h, names_to = "space", values_to = "conc") |>
    dplyr::mutate(arm = label)
}
s2b <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tumor_long(m_conv, "Conventional (Table 1 tvf_in_dox)"),
  tumor_long(m_conv_code, "Conventional (model-code tvf_in_dox)"),
  tumor_long(m_lipo, "Liposomal")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!(arm != "Liposomal" & grepl("liposomes", space)), h > 0)
ggplot(s2b, aes(h, conc, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~space, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 168)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (nM doxorubicin)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Replicates Supplementary Figure S2B of Hendriks 2012 (mouse, 3 mg/kg
conventional doxorubicin or PLD). The values below were read off that
figure by the maintainers.

```{r mouse-s2b-table}
at_h <- function(d, col, h) d[[col]][which.min(abs(d$h - h))]
peak <- function(d, col) max(d[[col]])
peak_h <- function(d, col) d$h[which.max(d[[col]])]
# First time after the peak at which a curve falls below `level`; NA when
# the curve never reaches that level.
cross_down_h <- function(d, col, level) {
  if (max(d[[col]]) < level) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  i <- which(d$h > d$h[which.max(d[[col]])] & d[[col]] < level)[1]
  d$h[i]
}
s2b_check <- data.frame(
  Readout = c(
    "Conventional: interstitium dox at 1 h (nM)",
    "Conventional: cell free dox falls below 1000 nM (h)",
    "Conventional: cell free dox at 24 h (nM)",
    "Liposomal: capillary liposomes at 48 h (nM dox eq.)",
    "Liposomal: capillary liposomes at 72 h (nM dox eq.)",
    "Liposomal: interstitium liposome peak (nM dox eq.)",
    "Liposomal: cell free dox peak (nM)",
    "Liposomal: cell DNA-bound dox peak (nM)"
  ),
  `Figure S2B` = c(140, 8.5, 270, 2800, 600, 2550, 740, 960),
  `Table 1 values` = c(
    at_h(m_conv, "c_int_tumor_dox", 1),
    cross_down_h(m_conv, "c_cell_tumor_free", 1000),
    at_h(m_conv, "c_cell_tumor_free", 24),
    at_h(m_lipo, "c_cap_tumor_lipo", 48),
    at_h(m_lipo, "c_cap_tumor_lipo", 72),
    peak(m_lipo, "c_int_tumor_lipo"),
    peak(m_lipo, "c_cell_tumor_free"),
    peak(m_lipo, "c_cell_tumor_bound")
  ),
  `Model-code tvf_in_dox` = c(
    at_h(m_conv_code, "c_int_tumor_dox", 1),
    cross_down_h(m_conv_code, "c_cell_tumor_free", 1000),
    at_h(m_conv_code, "c_cell_tumor_free", 24),
    NA, NA, NA, NA, NA
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(s2b_check, digits = 1)
```

The capillary liposome curve, which is set by the liposome PK alone,
reproduces the figure. The conventional-doxorubicin panels reproduce the
figure when the tumor influx flux is the one written in the published model
code (6.23e-5 dm/min, described there as a Ktrans-based value) rather than
the Table 1 estimate (2.96e-4 cm/min = 2.96e-5 dm/min); with the Table 1
value the tumor interstitium and cell concentrations are about half as high
and the free cell concentration never reaches 1000 nM (NA in the table).
The packaged mouse model uses the Table 1 value, which is also the nominal
point plotted in Figure 5a (see Errata). The liposomal tumor panels are not
reproduced exactly: the simulated interstitial liposome concentration peaks
earlier (about 12 h against about 19 h) and higher (3300 against 2550 nM),
and the cell concentrations are about 1.7-fold higher than in the figure.
No single published parameter explains the difference, and the packaged
values were not adjusted.

```{r mouse-s2b-checks}
stopifnot(
  # Liposome PK in blood/capillary: set by kel_lipo + krel_plasma.
  abs(at_h(m_lipo, "c_cap_tumor_lipo", 48) / 2800 - 1) < 0.25,
  # Conventional arm with the model-code influx flux reproduces S2B.
  abs(at_h(m_conv_code, "c_int_tumor_dox", 1) / 140 - 1) < 0.25,
  abs(at_h(m_conv_code, "c_cell_tumor_free", 24) / 270 - 1) < 0.25,
  # Liposomal arm: same order of magnitude as S2B (see text above).
  peak(m_lipo, "c_cell_tumor_bound") > 500,
  peak(m_lipo, "c_cell_tumor_bound") < 2500
)
```

# Mouse: plasma and tumor percent injected dose (Figure 3a, b, d, e)

```{r mouse-pid, fig.height = 6}
pid <- function(d, dose_nmol) {
  dose_ug <- dose_nmol * mw_dox / 1e3
  d |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      h,
      `Plasma total doxorubicin (%ID/mL)` = 100 * Cc / 1e3 / dose_nmol,
      `Tumor total doxorubicin (%ID/g)` = 100 * tumor_total_dox / dose_ug,
      `Tumor total liposome label (%ID/g)` = 100 * tumor_total_lipid / dose_ug
    )
}
fig3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pid(m_conv, mouse_dose(3)) |> dplyr::mutate(arm = "Conventional doxorubicin"),
  pid(m_lipo, mouse_dose(3)) |> dplyr::mutate(arm = "PLD")
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(h, arm), names_to = "readout", values_to = "value") |>
  dplyr::filter(!(arm == "Conventional doxorubicin" & grepl("liposome", readout)), h > 0)
ggplot(fig3, aes(h, value, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~readout, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Typical-value curves corresponding to the mean fits of Figure 3a, b (plasma)
and 3d, e (tumor). At time zero the plasma holds 100% of the dose in the
1.2 mL blood volume (83 %ID/mL), as in Figure 3a, b. The simulated PLD tumor
deposition peaks at about 7 %ID/g near 22 h, against about 4.6 %ID/g near
36 h for the mean fit drawn in Figure 3e, in line with the faster and higher
liposome deposition seen against Supplementary Figure S2B.

# Human: tumor compartments after 40 mg/m^2 (Supplementary Figure S2C)

```{r human-sim}
h_conv <- solve_one(mod_human, "central", human_dose(40), dur = 60)
h_lipo <- solve_one(mod_human, "central_lipo", human_dose(40), dur = 60)
# Table 1 prints the human doxorubicin efflux flux as 8.45E-03 cm/min
# (8.45e-4 dm/min); the published model code uses 8.45e-5 dm/min.
h_lipo_t1 <- solve_one(mod_human, "central_lipo", human_dose(40), dur = 60, params = c(tvf_out_tumor_dox = 8.45e-4))
h_conv_t1 <- solve_one(mod_human, "central", human_dose(40), dur = 60, params = c(tvf_out_tumor_dox = 8.45e-4))
```

```{r human-s2c, fig.height = 6}
s2c <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tumor_long(h_conv, "Conventional"),
  tumor_long(h_lipo, "Liposomal")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!(arm == "Conventional" & grepl("liposomes", space)), h > 0)
ggplot(s2c, aes(h, conc, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~space, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 168, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (nM doxorubicin)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Replicates Supplementary Figure S2C of Hendriks 2012 (human, 40 mg/m^2 of
conventional doxorubicin or PLD as a 60-minute infusion). Figure values were
read off the figure by the maintainers.

```{r human-s2c-table}
s2c_check <- data.frame(
  Readout = c(
    "Conventional: capillary dox at end of infusion (nM)",
    "Conventional: interstitium dox at 2 h (nM)",
    "Conventional: cell free dox peak (nM)",

    "Liposomal: capillary liposomes at 1 h (nM dox eq.)",

    "Liposomal: interstitium dox peak (nM)",
    "Liposomal: cell free dox peak (nM)",
    "Liposomal: cell DNA-bound dox peak (nM)"
  ),

    at_h(h_conv, "c_int_tumor_dox", 2),
    peak(h_conv, "c_cell_tumor_free"),
    peak(h_conv, "c_cell_tumor_bound"),
    at_h(h_lipo, "c_cap_tumor_lipo", 1),
    at_h(h_lipo, "c_cap_tumor_lipo", 168),

    peak(h_lipo, "c_cell_tumor_free"),

  ),
  `Table 1 tvf_out_dox` = c(
    at_h(h_conv_t1, "c_cap_tumor_dox", 1),
    at_h(h_conv_t1, "c_int_tumor_dox", 2),
    peak(h_conv_t1, "c_cell_tumor_free"),
    peak(h_conv_t1, "c_cell_tumor_bound"),

    peak(h_lipo_t1, "c_cell_tumor_bound")

  check.names = FALSE

s2c_check$`% diff (packaged)` <- 100 * (s2c_check$`Packaged model` / s2c_check$`Figure S2C` - 1)
knitr::kable(s2c_check, digits = 1)
```

Every panel of Supplementary Figure S2C is reproduced to within the reading
precision of the figure by the packaged human model. With the
Table 1 value of `tvf_out_dox` the interstitial and cellular doxorubicin
levels drop roughly ten-fold below the figure, which is why the packaged
model uses the model-code value (Errata).

```{r human-s2c-checks}
stopifnot(
  abs(s2c_check$`% diff (packaged)`) < 15
)
```

# Human: PLD plasma PK (Figure 3h)

```{r human-pld-pk}
h_lipo_long <- solve_one(
  mod_human, "central_lipo", human_dose(40), dur = 60,
  times = c(0, 60, seq(360, 240 * 60, by = 360))
)
pld_pid <- data.frame(h = h_lipo_long$h, pid = 100 * h_lipo_long$Cc_lipid_total / 1e3 / human_dose(40))
ggplot(dplyr::filter(pld_pid, h > 0), aes(h, pid)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 240, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma liposome label (%ID/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates the shape of Figure 3h (111In-PLD plasma PK, Harrington et al.):
the plasma liposome label starts near 0.02 %ID/mL (one dose in 4.85 L of
blood) and falls mono-exponentially with a half-life of about 2.9 days.

```{r human-pld-pk-check}
stopifnot(
  abs(at_h(pld_pid, "pid", 1) / 0.02 - 1) < 0.1
)
```

# Half-lives with PKNCA

The paper states that the PLD plasma half-life is about 10 h in the mouse
against 2-3 days in humans. PKNCA half-lives of the simulated plasma total
doxorubicin (`Cc`, free plus liposome-encapsulated) check this statement.
(Its other PK statement, that doxorubicin elimination is about four-fold
slower in humans than in mice, is a direct property of the Table 1 rate
constants: `kel` 0.36 against 0.082 1/min.)

```{r pknca}
nca_in <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  m_conv |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Mouse, free doxorubicin 3 mg/kg"),
  m_lipo |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Mouse, PLD 3 mg/kg"),
  h_conv |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Human, free doxorubicin 40 mg/m2"),
  h_lipo |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "Human, PLD 40 mg/m2")
) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, time_h = time / 60) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))
dose_df <- data.frame(
  treatment = unique(nca_in$treatment),
  id = 1L,
  time_h = 0,
  dose = c(mouse_dose(3), mouse_dose(3), human_dose(40), human_dose(40))
)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in, Cc ~ time_h | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time_h | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "half.life", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Treatment = treatment,
    `Cmax (nM)` = cmax,
    `Terminal t1/2 (h)` = half.life,
    `AUC0-168 h (nM x h)` = auclast
  )
knitr::kable(nca_tbl, digits = 2)
```

```{r nca-comparison}
reference <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Mouse, PLD 3 mg/kg", "Human, PLD 40 mg/m2"),
  half.life = c(10, 2.5 * 24)
)
cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res,
  reference,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "half.life",
  units = c(half.life = "h")
)
knitr::kable(cmp)
```

The reference PLD half-lives are the paper's narrative values (Results,
'Human scale-up': "2-3 days vs. 10 h"); the human reference is the middle of
the 2-3 day range. The simulated human PLD half-life (about 51 h over the
first week) sits inside that range; the simulated mouse PLD half-life
(about 10 h) matches the mouse value.

```{r nca-checks}
hl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life")
hl_of <- function(x) hl$PPORRES[hl$treatment == x]
stopifnot(
  hl_of("Mouse, PLD 3 mg/kg") > 8, hl_of("Mouse, PLD 3 mg/kg") < 12,
  hl_of("Human, PLD 40 mg/m2") > 48, hl_of("Human, PLD 40 mg/m2") < 72
)
```

# Relative delivery of PLD vs conventional doxorubicin (Figure 5)

Figure 5 compares the area under the DNA-bound doxorubicin curve after PLD
with that after conventional doxorubicin across a grid of tumor influx
fluxes for free drug (`tvf_in_dox`) and liposomes (`tvf_in_lipo`). In the
mouse, 3 mg/kg of each was given and the AUC taken over one week; in humans,
60 mg/m^2 of doxorubicin every 3 weeks was compared with 50 mg/m^2 of PLD
every 4 weeks over 3 weeks (one dose of each). The grid below is coarser
than the published contour plot.

```{r fig5-grid}
grid_ratio <- function(mod, dose_conv, dose_lipo, dur, t_end_min, tvf_dox_cm, tvf_lipo_cm) {
  g <- expand.grid(tvf_dox_cm = tvf_dox_cm, tvf_lipo_cm = tvf_lipo_cm)
  g$id <- seq_len(nrow(g))
  pars <- data.frame(
    id = g$id,
    tvf_in_tumor_dox = g$tvf_dox_cm / 10,
    tvf_in_tumor_lipo = g$tvf_lipo_cm / 10
  )
  times <- seq(0, t_end_min, by = 30)
  auc <- function(cmt, amt) {
    ev <- rxode2::et(amt = amt, cmt = cmt, dur = dur) |>
      rxode2::et(times, cmt = "central") |>
      rxode2::et(id = g$id)
    out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, params = pars, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8))
    nca_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
      dplyr::select(out, id, time, tumor_dna_dox),
      tumor_dna_dox ~ time | id
    )
    nca_int <- data.frame(start = 0, end = t_end_min, auclast = TRUE)
    res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(nca_conc, intervals = nca_int))
    as.data.frame(res$result) |>
      dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
      dplyr::select(id, PPORRES)
  }
  a_conv <- auc("central", dose_conv)
  a_lipo <- auc("central_lipo", dose_lipo)
  g |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::rename(a_conv, auc_conv = PPORRES), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::rename(a_lipo, auc_lipo = PPORRES), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(log10_ratio = log10(auc_lipo / auc_conv))
}
tvf_dox_axis <- 10^seq(-4, -2, by = 0.5)
tvf_lipo_axis <- 10^seq(-7, -4.5, by = 0.5)
fig5_mouse <- grid_ratio(
  mod_mouse, mouse_dose(3), mouse_dose(3), dur = 0, t_end_min = 7 * 1440,
  tvf_dox_cm = c(tvf_dox_axis, 2.96e-4), tvf_lipo_cm = c(tvf_lipo_axis, 2.64e-6)
)
fig5_human <- grid_ratio(
  mod_human, human_dose(60), human_dose(50), dur = 60, t_end_min = 21 * 1440,
  tvf_dox_cm = c(tvf_dox_axis, 3.63e-3), tvf_lipo_cm = c(tvf_lipo_axis, 2.64e-6)
)
```

```{r fig5-plot, fig.height = 4}
fig5 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(fig5_mouse, species = "Mouse, 3 mg/kg each"),
  dplyr::mutate(fig5_human, species = "Human, 60 mg/m2 dox vs 50 mg/m2 PLD")
)
ggplot(
  dplyr::filter(fig5, tvf_dox_cm %in% tvf_dox_axis, tvf_lipo_cm %in% tvf_lipo_axis),
  aes(tvf_dox_cm, tvf_lipo_cm, fill = log10_ratio)
) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", log10_ratio)), size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "grey85", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~species) +
  labs(
    x = "tvf_in_dox (cm/min)", y = "tvf_in_lipo (cm/min)",
    fill = "log10(AUC PLD /\nAUC dox)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figure 5a, b of Hendriks 2012 on a coarse grid. As in the paper,
liposomal delivery wins most clearly at high liposome and low free-drug
permeability (upper left), the advantage falls as free-drug permeability
rises, and at low liposome permeability conventional doxorubicin delivers
more drug to DNA. At the nominal parameter values (Table 1), PLD delivers
about six-fold more doxorubicin to tumor DNA than conventional doxorubicin
in the mouse (log10 ratio 0.76, in the red region of Figure 5a) but only
about 2.5-fold more in humans (0.40, in the yellow band of Figure 5b), the
paper's central contrast between the species.

```{r fig5-nominal}
nominal <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fig5_mouse |>
    dplyr::filter(tvf_dox_cm == 2.96e-4, tvf_lipo_cm == 2.64e-6) |>
    dplyr::mutate(species = "Mouse"),
  fig5_human |>
    dplyr::filter(tvf_dox_cm == 3.63e-3, tvf_lipo_cm == 2.64e-6) |>
    dplyr::mutate(species = "Human")
)
knitr::kable(
  nominal |>
    dplyr::select(species, tvf_dox_cm, tvf_lipo_cm, log10_ratio) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      tvf_dox_cm = formatC(tvf_dox_cm, format = "e", digits = 2),
      tvf_lipo_cm = formatC(tvf_lipo_cm, format = "e", digits = 2)
    ) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      Species = species,
      `tvf_in_dox (cm/min)` = tvf_dox_cm,
      `tvf_in_lipo (cm/min)` = tvf_lipo_cm,
      `log10(AUC PLD / AUC dox)` = log10_ratio
    ),
  digits = 2
)
stopifnot(
  # Mouse nominal point lies in the red region of Figure 5a (0.5 to 1.25).
  nominal$log10_ratio[nominal$species == "Mouse"] > 0.5,
  nominal$log10_ratio[nominal$species == "Mouse"] < 1.25,
  # Human nominal point lies in the yellow / grey band of Figure 5b.
  nominal$log10_ratio[nominal$species == "Human"] > -0.25,
  nominal$log10_ratio[nominal$species == "Human"] < 0.75
)
```

# Liposome release rate (Figure 6c)

Figure 6c varies the three liposome release rates together (0.01-100 times
nominal) after 40 mg/m^2 PLD in the human model and shows that delivery to
DNA is greatest near the nominal release rates: too slow and the liposomes
are cleared before releasing their drug, too fast and PLD behaves like free
drug.

```{r fig6c}
mult <- 10^seq(-2, 2, by = 0.5)
rel <- lapply(mult, function(k) {
  d <- solve_one(
    mod_human, "central_lipo", human_dose(40), dur = 60,
    params = c(krel_plasma = 5.465e-5 * k, krel_tissue = 1.77e-4 * k, krel_cell = 9.6e-4 * k),
    times = seq(0, 21 * 1440, by = 60)
  )
  data.frame(multiplier = k, time = d$time, tumor_dna_dox = d$tumor_dna_dox)
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()
rel_auc <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(rel, tumor_dna_dox ~ time | multiplier),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 21 * 1440, auclast = TRUE)
))
rel_tbl <- as.data.frame(rel_auc$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(multiplier, auc = PPORRES)
ggplot(rel_tbl, aes(multiplier, auc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Release-rate multiplier (krel_plasma, krel_tumor, krel_cell)",
    y = "AUC DNA-bound doxorubicin (ug/g x min)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
best <- rel_tbl$multiplier[which.max(rel_tbl$auc)]
best
stopifnot(best >= 0.1, best <= 10)
```

Replicates the conclusion of Figure 6c: on this grid DNA-bound exposure is
greatest at the nominal PLD release rates (multiplier 1).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Mouse `tvf_in_dox`.** Table 1 gives the fitted mouse value
  2.96E-04 cm/min, which is also the nominal value plotted in Figure 5a. The
  published model code and its workbook instead carry 6.23e-5 dm/min
  (6.23E-04 cm/min), labelled there as a Ktrans-based value, and
  Supplementary Figure S2B was evidently generated with it (its
  conventional-doxorubicin panels are reproduced with that value above).
  The packaged mouse model uses the Table 1 estimate; use
  `ini(tvf_in_tumor_dox = 6.23e-5)` to reproduce Supplementary Figure S2B.
* **Human `tvf_out_dox`.** Table 1 prints 8.45E-03 cm/min, whereas both the
  human SBML model and the human workbook give 8.45e-5 dm/min
  (8.45E-04 cm/min; "average of 10, 20 and 40 mg/m2 fits" to Northfelt et
  al.). Every other length-based value in Table 1 is the code value times
  ten, and only the code value reproduces Supplementary Figure S2C (the
  Table 1 value lowers tumor doxorubicin about ten-fold), so Table 1 is
  taken to carry a factor-of-ten conversion slip and the packaged model uses
  8.45e-5 dm/min.
* **Human liposome PK.** The human SBML file carries a two-compartment
  liposome model (`k12_lipo = 0.0018`, `k21_lipo = 0.00341`,
  `kel_lipo = 5.4e-4` 1/min), apparently the Northfelt-data variant the
  Methods mention. Table 1, the human workbook (`k12_lipo = 0`,
  `kel_lipo = 1.689e-4`) and Supplementary Figure S2C all use the
  one-compartment model, which the packaged model follows with Table 1's
  `kel_lipo = 1.67e-4` 1/min. The peripheral liposome compartment is kept
  but switched off (`k12_lipo = 0`); setting `k12_lipo = 0.0018` and
  `kel_lipo = 5.4e-4` reproduces the SBML variant.
* **Human `tvf_in_lipo`.** The human model carries the mouse value
  (2.64E-06 cm/min), as Table 1 and the model code do. The paper estimated
  this flux per patient (Figure 3l, Figure 5b squares), and Figure 5b draws
  the free-drug estimates at about 1.2E-06 cm/min; the value should be
  varied for patient- or tumor-specific simulations.
* **Tumor geometry.** Table 1 lists a 5 um capillary radius and a fractional
  vascular volume of 0.070. The model code computes the capillary surface
  area from a radius distribution (3, 5, 7 um with fractions 0.1, 0.6, 0.2;
  effective radius 4.7 um) and the vascular fraction from that distribution
  plus 23 um arterioles (0.062); the packaged models follow the code. The
  Table 1 'cell to interstitium ratio' of 0.412 is used, as in the code, as
  the cellular fraction of the non-vascular volume.
* **Heart sub-model.** The heart compartments, their parameters and
  `kdeg_dox` come only from the published model code and workbooks (the
  companion cardiac work); the paper text does not describe them. They are
  kept because the published model includes them and their blood flow
  returns drug to the circulation.
* **P-glycoprotein efflux.** The model code contains a Michaelis-Menten
  P-gp efflux reaction with `Pgp_Vmax = 0`; the paper states that P-gp was
  not represented. The inactive reaction is omitted.
* **Unused model-code quantities.** The liposome projected area, the
  intercapillary radii and the reverse membrane rate constants `kr_ol`,
  `kr_il` are defined in the code but never used in a rate law; they are
  omitted.
* **Dose units.** Doses are in nmol of doxorubicin (PLD: nmol of
  encapsulated doxorubicin); mg/kg and mg/m^2 doses are converted with the
  code's molecular weight of 580 g/mol and a 0.02 kg mouse or 1.8 m^2
  patient.
* **In vitro cellular-uptake model.** The paper also applied the cellular
  sub-model on its own to doxorubicin uptake in 21 cell lines (Figure 2).
  Only histograms of the per-cell-line estimates are reported and the
  incubation geometry (cells per well, medium volume) is not, so that
  application is not packaged separately; its median parameters are the
  cellular parameters of both models.
* **Figure 3 representative fits.** Figure 3j and 3k show single-patient
  fits with patient-specific `tvf_out_dox` or `tvf_in_lipo`; these are not
  reproducible from the typical values and are not replicated.
